key_insight: Learn the dissipation potential with a convex, frame-indifferent neural network so the constitutive law remains physically well-posed while fitting only velocity data.
engineering_relevance: This gives a safer way to identify complex-fluid material laws from indirect measurements and improves robustness when transferring to new geometries or unstable flow regimes.
method: Use an input-convex neural network to represent the dissipation potential.
Enforce frame-indifference, evenness, and convexity by construction; penalize nonzero gradient at the origin for dissipativity.
Couple Firedrake and PyTorch to solve the PDE-constrained inverse problem and compute the loss gradient.
evidence_signal: The approach was tested on four benchmarks: compressible Navier-Stokes, Herschel-Bulkley flow, Hibler sea-ice rheology, and DEM data, showing recovery of known physics, geometric transfer, and improved stability where unstructured methods diverge.
watch_item: The method depends on careful symmetrization and weak dissipation enforcement, so training and implementation may be sensitive near very small strain rates.
paper_title: Well-posed by Design: Learning Constitutive Laws from Velocity Data using Convex Neural Network Potentials
